papers.title: Experimental observation of dynamical blockade between transmon qubits via ZZ interaction engineering
papers.abstract: We report the experimental realization of strong longitudinal (ZZ) coupling between two superconducting transmon qubits achieved solely through capacitive engineering. By systematically varying the qubit frequency detuning, we measure cross-Kerr inter-qubit interaction strengths ranging from 10 MHz up to 350 MHz, more than an order of magnitude larger than previously observed in similar capacitively coupled systems. In this configuration, the qubits enter a strong-interaction regime in which the excitation of one qubit inhibits that of its neighbor, demonstrating a dynamical blockade mediated entirely by the engineered ZZ coupling. Circuit quantization simulations accurately reproduce the experimental results, while perturbative models confirm the theoretical origin of the energy shift as a hybridization between the computational states and higher-excitation manifolds. We establish a robust and scalable method to access interaction-dominated physics in superconducting circuits, providing a pathway towards solid-state implementations of globally controlled quantum architectures and cooperative many-body dynamics.

similar_to.title: Suppression of static ZZ interaction in an all-transmon quantum processor
Suppression of crosstalk in superconducting qubits using dynamical decoupling

summary.summary: This paper demonstrates strong ZZ coupling between capacitively coupled transmon qubits, achieving cross-Kerr interaction strengths up to 350 MHz—more than an order of magnitude larger than prior capacitive implementations—and uses this to observe a dynamical blockade effect analogous to Rydberg-atom dipole blockade. The engineered longitudinal interaction enables interaction-dominated physics in superconducting circuits suitable for globally controlled quantum architectures.
summary.motivation: Rydberg atoms achieve strong collective phenomena through large state-dependent interactions, but superconducting qubits typically have weak intrinsic ZZ coupling. The authors sought to engineer strong longitudinal interactions purely through capacitive coupling to realize blockade-mediated physics and globally controlled quantum operations without increasing control line complexity.
summary.method: Two transmon qubits were fabricated with direct capacitive coupling ($C_{12} = 5.11$ fF). The ZZ interaction strength $\zeta(\Delta)$ was characterized via two-tone spectroscopy and Ramsey interferometry as a function of qubit detuning $\Delta$, and blockade was demonstrated by applying sequential $\pi$-pulses with variable delay. Black-box circuit quantization and Schrieffer–Wolff perturbation theory explained the results.
summary.result: The measured $\zeta$ ranged from $10$ MHz at $\Delta/(2\pi) = 2$ GHz to $350$ MHz near resonance, scaling as $\propto J^2/\Delta$ where $J/(2\pi) \approx 240$ MHz. Blockade was observed: exciting Q2 first suppressed Q1 excitation with $\zeta/(2\pi) = 19$ MHz, with suppression lifting on the $T_1$ timescale of Q2 ($\sim 8$ μs for chip 1). Results validated on a second device with X-mon geometry and comparable coherence ($T_1 \sim 15$ μs, $T_2^{\mathrm{echo}} \sim 20$ μs).

papers.title: Single-shot Quantum State Classification via Nonlinear Quantum Amplification
papers.abstract: Quantum amplifiers are intrinsically nonlinear systems whose performance limits are set by quantum mechanics. In quantum measurement, amplifier operation is conventionally optimized in the linear regime by maximizing signal-to-noise ratio, an objective that is well-suited to parameter estimation but is typically insufficient for more general tasks such as arbitrary quantum state discrimination. Here we show that single-shot quantum state classification can benefit from operating a quantum amplifier outside the linear regime, when the measurement chain is optimized end-to-end for a task-specific cost function. We analyze a realistic superconducting readout architecture that includes state preparation, cryogenic nonlinear amplification, and room-temperature detection with finite noise. By introducing performance metrics tailored to state discrimination, we identify operating regimes in which nonlinear amplification provides a measurable advantage and clarify the trade-offs that ultimately limit classification fidelity. Building on these results, we propose a qubit readout architecture without cavity displacement that exploits nonlinear amplification to enhance single-shot state discrimination performance. Our results establish the practical value of nonlinear quantum amplifiers for quantum state discrimination and lay the foundation for a broader program to develop a general, end-to-end framework for resource-constrained optimization of nonlinear amplification in quantum information processing tasks.

similar_to.title: Introduction to Quantum Noise, Measurement and Amplification
Model-based Optimization of Superconducting Qubit Readout

summary.summary: This work demonstrates that operating cryogenic quantum amplifiers in the nonlinear regime, rather than optimizing for linear quantum-limited performance, can enhance single-shot quantum state classification when the measurement chain is end-to-end optimized for task-specific objectives. The analysis uses two coupled SNAIL oscillators—a squeezer for state preparation and a nonlinear analyzer—and shows that exploiting Kerr nonlinearity to transduce information encoded in higher-order moments achieves classification fidelities approaching unity in regimes where linear amplification fails.
summary.motivation: Conventional cryogenic readout chains optimize amplifier performance by maximizing signal-to-noise ratio in the linear regime, an objective well-suited for parameter estimation but suboptimal for quantum state discrimination tasks. This work investigates whether deliberate nonlinear amplifier operation can provide practical advantages for measurement tasks beyond parameter estimation, grounded in superconducting qubit readout architectures.
summary.method: A two-SNAIL system with unidirectional coupling was modeled via a stochastic quantum master equation with third- and fourth-order nonlinearities. State discrimination between squeezed vacuum states with orthogonal squeezing directions was analyzed using truncated cumulant equations of motion, performance metrics (mean separation and Fisher discriminant), and end-to-end optimization over externally tunable pump and signal drive strengths and phases, with numerical solutions validated against analytical perturbative expressions in the weak-nonlinearity limit.
summary.result: Optimal nonlinear operation achieved classification fidelity of 1.0 (versus 0.84 for linear operation) for zero-mean pointer states distinguished only by second moments. The optimal dispersive shift for qubit readout without cavity displacement was found to be $\chi \approx 0.2\kappa$, substantially lower than the conventional $\chi_\mathrm{opt,disp} = \kappa/2$, and performance degraded gracefully with downstream classical noise $n_\mathrm{cl}$ from room-temperature electronics.

papers.title: Scalable and telecom single-erbium system with record-long room-temperature quantum coherence
papers.abstract: Eliminating cryogenic operating requirements while preserving microsecond-scale quantum coherence and enabling CMOS scalability remains a central challenge for telecom quantum technologies. Addressing this, we introduce a CMOS-compatible quantum system comprising single-erbium-(Er)-ion qudits (five-level systems) operating across the visible and telecom C-band. Through innovative nanofabrication, we achieve self-aligned ion placement, enabling spatial isolation of single-Er ions and suppressing dephasing. We realize individually addressable single-Er-devices with record-long optical coherence times in the telecom C-band exceeding 500 μs at ambient conditions, a performance previously limited to vacuum conditions at temperatures over 900 times lower. Furthermore, we present the first demonstration of background-free, upconversion-enabled single-photon Er-emissions providing coherent, high-contrast optical readouts. This work showcases the first room-temperature single-Er-qudit system with unprecedented properties enabling next-generation cryogen-free telecom quantum technologies.

summary.summary: Single Er$^{3+}$ ions in a CMOS-compatible platform achieve record optical coherence times exceeding 500 μs in the telecom C-band at room temperature, surpassing previously cryogenic-only performance. Background-free upconversion-enabled single-photon readout and self-aligned nanofabrication enable scalable, individually addressable Er-qudits (five-level systems) without cryogenic cooling.
summary.motivation: Telecom quantum technologies require long quantum coherence at ambient conditions while maintaining CMOS compatibility and scalability, eliminating the need for cryogenic infrastructure.
summary.method: Self-aligned nanofabrication was used to spatially isolate individual Er$^{3+}$ ions, suppressing dephasing, with upconversion-based single-photon readout in the visible band to detect coherent transitions in the C-band.
summary.result: Optical coherence times exceed 500 μs at room temperature in the telecom C-band—a 900× improvement over prior vacuum-based systems at millikelvin temperatures—with background-free readout and demonstrated individual addressability.
